task_description: A GAIA web-research question: 'According to Google Finance, when was the first year the Apple stock went above $50 (without adjusting for stock split)?' The gold answer is 2018. The question is notoriously mis-worded: Google Finance shows split-ADJUSTED prices by default, so 'according to Google Finance' the first year the displayed chart crosses $50 is 2018 (the split-adjusted series), even though the question's parenthetical literally says 'without adjusting.' The gold (2018) reflects the value a user reading the Google Finance chart would actually see; the true unadjusted-price crossing of $50 happened decades earlier (1980s).
final_vs_expected: produced None (run hit the message cap with no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 2018 - team converged internally on 1987 (the literal unadjusted crossing) but never finalized; both the un-emitted candidate (1987) and the emitted-nothing are off from the chart-based gold 2018.
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: the team got stuck in an unbreakable loop demanding 'direct Google Finance evidence' that the tools could never retrieve, so the selector re-routed to WebResearcher ~25 times until the message cap, never reaching a Finalizer that would emit an answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions) is primary: neither the selector, the Finalizer, nor WebResearcher recognized that the Google-Finance-direct evidence was unobtainable and that the team should either finalize on best available evidence or finalize a graceful 'cannot verify' answer; instead they looped to the message cap with no FINAL ANSWER (Turn 11 & 24 Finalizer both REFUSE to finalize: 'without that, I can't finalize'). 1.3 (step repetition): Turns 4-10 and 16-29 are near-verbatim re-publications of the same 'supported: 1987 / not direct Google Finance' message with no new action; Turn 23 literally duplicates the same block twice within one message. 1.4 (loss of context): WebResearcher's round-1 search (Turn 1) surfaced the gaia-benchmark thread that explained the entire split-adjustment trap and that 'according to Google Finance' implies the adjusted series, but this decisive context was dropped and never re-engaged. 3.1 borderline-inverse: the run did NOT terminate prematurely on a wrong answer; it failed to terminate at all, so I tag 1.5 over 3.1, but note the verification demand became a non-terminating gate. No 2.x inter-agent-misalignment code earns its place: the private reasoning and published messages are consistently aligned (agents say privately 'I can't get it' and publish exactly that).
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher runs 4 rounds of searches and fetches 1stock1 + Digrin yearly tables. Its very first search returns the gaia-benchmark/leaderboard thread stating plainly that 'Google Finance adjusts for stock splits by default... the first year Apple's stock went above $50 (adjusting for splits)' and that the unadjusted crossing was '>10 years earlier' and 'the question is simply wrong.' WebResearcher ignores the adjusted interpretation, reads the 1stock1 unadjusted table (1986 ending $40.50, 1987 ending $84.00) and publishes that Apple 'first went above $50 unadjusted for stock splits in 1987' with third-party sources, conceding no direct Google Finance source. Turn 2: Critic correctly notes the question said 'According to Google Finance' but no Google Finance evidence was provided, and demands a direct Google Finance source. Turns 3-10: WebResearcher repeatedly agrees ('You're right'), re-scopes the claim to '1987, supported by third-party, not Google-Finance-verified,' and re-posts essentially the same paragraph ~7 times; selector keeps re-picking WebResearcher. Turn 11: Finalizer, instead of finalizing, re-issues the Critic's request: 'Need direct Google Finance evidence from WebResearcher.' Turn 12: WebResearcher actually fetches a Google Finance Apple URL but gets only the live quote/chart UI (no historical series) and honestly reports it can't extract history. Turns 13-23: the loop continues - WebResearcher re-publishes 'can't get direct Google Finance evidence, third-party still supports 1987' verbatim many times (Turn 23 duplicates the block twice). Turn 15 Critic re-reviews and again demands direct Google Finance evidence. Turn 24: Finalizer again refuses to finalize ('without that, I can't finalize the Google Finance-specific answer'). Turns 25-29: more identical 'unverified' re-posts until the run hits the ~30-message cap with NO FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is a clean structural non-convergence / termination failure, NOT inter-agent misalignment. The Critic raised a legitimate gap (no direct Google Finance evidence) at Turn 2, but the team treated 'produce direct Google Finance historical evidence' as a hard precondition for finalizing - and that evidence was literally unobtainable with the available tools (Google Finance's historical chart is a JS widget that fetch_url cannot read; the team confirmed this at Turn 12). With no agent empowered to say 'the evidence is unobtainable, finalize on best-available' or 'finalize that we cannot verify,' the system entered a non-terminating verification gate: Critic/Finalizer demand evidence -> selector routes to WebResearcher -> WebResearcher re-reports failure -> repeat, ~25 cycles, until the message cap. Two deeper failures compound it: (1) a capability/comprehension miss - WebResearcher's FIRST search surfaced the exact key to the puzzle (Google Finance is split-adjusted, so 'according to Google Finance' = the adjusted series, which crosses $50 ~2018), but the team locked onto the literal 'without adjusting' phrasing and pursued the unadjusted 1987 answer, discarding the adjusted reading that the gold (2018) actually rewards; (2) the Finalizer never exercises its role - twice (Turns 11, 24) it had the floor and could have emitted FINAL ANSWER: 1987 (best-supported) or a hedged answer, but instead it punted back to WebResearcher, so the run produced nothing. The selector is the proximate engine of non-convergence: from Turn 13 onward its reasoning repeatedly acknowledges 'the web researcher already tried... maybe one more chance... unlikely' (Turn 27) yet keeps routing to WebResearcher anyway, never to Finalizer-with-a-mandate-to-conclude.
reasoning_vs_published: Private reasoning and published messages are tightly ALIGNED throughout - there is no 2.4/2.6 gap. At Turn 12 round 3 WebResearcher privately reasons 'I'll need to say no direct evidence was found' and publishes exactly that. At Turn 25 it privately reasons 'Being honest about my resources is important... whether I should stick to what I already know' and publishes a faithful 'I don't have direct Google Finance historical evidence.' At Turn 29 it reasons 'I should be honest and acknowledge that I can't provide that' and does so. The Finalizer at Turn 11 privately reasons 'I should pause here and request help from WebResearcher' and publishes precisely a request to WebResearcher - reasoning and action match (it is a role/termination failure, not a mismatch). The one genuinely lost signal is NOT a private-vs-published distortion but a dropped tool finding: WebResearcher's Turn-1 search result (the gaia-benchmark thread: 'Google Finance adjusts for stock splits by default... the first year... (adjusting for splits)... the question is simply wrong') was the decisive clue to the gold (2018), and it was neither carried into reasoning nor published in a way that reframed the team's interpretation. The selector's reasoning is transparent about the misrouting and even self-aware of futility ('the web researcher has struggled in the past, but maybe I should give them one more chance? However, it seems unlikely' - Turn 27) yet it never converts that awareness into routing to a terminating action. So: no information distortion, no ignored peer correction (the Critic's correction was in fact heeded - too literally), no ToM failure between agents; the breakdown is structural (no exit from the verification loop) plus a shared comprehension miss on the split-adjustment trick.
